changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers who own month-end close (CFO, controller): Know where your money is. Every deposit ties back to its transactions and the invoice in your ERP, so month-end close stops being a week of archaeology. Use 'deposits', not 'payments' or 'payouts'.
changes.why: Payout reconciliation was the only part of the pitch that stopped the decider, and she described it as "I just want to know where my money is" and called month-end "a week of archaeology"; she never once said "payments", only "the deposits".

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers: Send us one month of your statements and we'll show you, in dollars, the hours your team spends matching deposits and what you write off from deposits that never get matched. Your number, not ours.
changes.why: The deal turned from "Dead, honestly" when Wen costed the matching work from one month of the controller's own statements, and the CFO valued it because it was "my number, not yours."

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance-led, domestic buyers whose IT team isn't building anything, stop opening with global growth, every currency, or 'financial infrastructure'. Open with the reworded M9 deposits line instead. Drop the M2 developer pitch for these buyers too.
changes.why: The rep ran the standard global, all-currencies deck for a customer that sells to restaurants in three states with a four-person IT team that isn't building anything, and "Nobody said 'infrastructure.'"

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: Add a wholesale or distribution customer story, plus a reference customer from that segment who will take a call, for distributor buyers. Don't offer retail stories as proof to these buyers.
changes.why: The CFO asked to talk to another distributor, dismissed the retail story with "this is a company that sells sweaters," and raised the missing reference twice even after signing.
